purpose: Candidate turns for the THREE failure patterns confirmed by ablation in probe.py / probe4.py / probe5.py. These are candidates, not data: collect.py runs each one through the real prompt path and the real model, and only the turns that actually reproduce the pattern become training examples. A turn that does not reproduce is recorded as a non-reproducer and kept out of the dataset.

P1_prose_confirmation.confirmed_by: probe4.py [J] - removing the sensitive-action Hard-rules block alone flips tg-01 to a correct call; probe3.py [H][I] rules out the tool schema's confirmation clause in both directions; probe5.py [M] rules out an additive prompt clarification.
P1_prose_confirmation.failure: A confirmation-gated send with every argument present is answered with a prose request for confirmation instead of the tool call, so the action never reaches the tool layer's gate at all.
P1_prose_confirmation.target: Emit the tool call. The gate fires inside the tool, after the call.

P2_speculative_search.confirmed_by: probe.py [D] - the fact-in-memory control answers correctly from the memory block, so memory reading works; the failure is specific to a fact the block does not contain. probe2.py [F] shows the model does NOT invent a time, it keeps searching.
P2_speculative_search.failure: A recall question whose answer is absent from the memory block is answered by searching whatever channel happens to be on the tool surface, instead of the honest 'I do not have a record of that' the memory block explicitly asks for.
P2_speculative_search.target: Plain text saying there is no record of it, naming what IS recorded.

P3_group_name_as_tool.confirmed_by: probe2.py [G] - 3/3 reproductions of {"tool": "whatsapp", ...}. 'whatsapp' is a TOOL GROUP key (toolGroups.ts:147) surfaced by the 'Also available, not listed above' sentence, not a tool. At runtime this falls through to the MCP fallback and returns 'Unknown tool', burning a turn.
P3_group_name_as_tool.failure: When the tool the request needs is not on the surface, the model emits the group name from the 'Also available' sentence as if it were a tool.
P3_group_name_as_tool.target: The plain-text response the prompt itself asks for: say the capability exists and ask the user to restate naming it.
